newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Ivory Coast privatises parts of Palmindustrie.
newsitem.headline: Ivory Coast privatises parts of Palmindustrie.

text.p: Ivory Coast has sold off a bloc of plantations, a hotel complex and an oil factory belonging to state agro-industrial giant Palmindustrie, which has been divided up into segments for privatisation.

The government said in a statement published on Friday that it had approved the sale of the Palm Club hotel complex, a palm oil factory at Vridi and the Assinie coconut plantations variously to Ivorian, foreign investors and a mix of the two.
Palmindustrie has a capital of 3.36 billion CFA and an annual turnover of around 60 billion CFA from coconut and palm oil plantations and associated processing plants.
The Ivorian company Assistance Contact International belonging to businessman Francois Bakou bought the Palm Club complex for 700 million CFA francs.
Franco-Ivoirian agro-industrial import-export company CAIMPEX brought the Assinie plantations for 900 million CFA francs.
The Swiss company IPS (Industriel Promotion Services) bought the Vridi factory in Abidjan for 3.3 billion CFA francs.
Last May, Ivory Coast launched an international offer for Palmindustrie's five oil palm blocks, including the Irobo/Boubo unit, and the Vridi palmkernel crushing factory.
One bloc of plantations at Irobo and Boubo in the central part of southern Ivory Coast had to be re-advertised because it attracted no bids. The other blocs remain to be sold.
Ivory Coast has sold off 35 of 58 companies earmarked for privatisation under plans to relaunch its economy.
